How do I use an original product photo and a marked-up reference image together for a targeted color edit? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
To perform a targeted color edit using an original product photo alongside a marked-up reference image, you can use either traditional color-matching workflows or modern Generative AI tools.
Depending on your software, here are the most effective workflows to combine these assets:
Method 1: The AI Generative Fill Workflow (Photoshop 2026)
If your marked-up reference image shows the exact target color or material on a similar object, you can utilize the AI Reference Image feature in Photoshop 2026: 
Isolate the Product: Open your original product photo and use the Object Selection Tool or Quick Selection Tool to select the specific area or part you want to recolor. 
YouTube
·PHLEARN
 +1
Activate Generative Fill: Click Generative Fill on the floating Contextual Task Bar. 
Phlearn
 +1
Upload the Reference Image: Click the Reference Image Icon next to the prompt box and drag or upload your marked-up reference photo. 
Phlearn
Configure Settings: Choose Reference to the object and select Swap the selected area. This tells the AI model (Adobe Firefly Fill & Expand) to analyze the colors and textures of your reference object rather than the entire frame. 
Adobe
 +2
Generate and Refine: Click Generate. Toggle through the variations in your Properties Panel, pick the best match, and click Enhance Detail to upscale it to match your original photo’s resolution.

Method 2: The Precise Eyedropper & Curves Workflow
If you want to manually transfer specific colors sampled from the marked-up reference image to targeted areas of the original product photo, follow this manual matching approach: 
YouTube
·Adobe Asia Pacific
Step 1: Sample the Targets: Open your marked-up reference photo. Use the Lasso tool to select the specific color-marked zones (e.g., highlights, midtones, and shadows). Apply a Filter > Blur > Average to each zone to get an even, single-color block of your target shade.
Step 2: Transfer to Main Photo: Copy these averaged color layers and paste them into your original product photo document as a temporary visual guide.
Step 3: Map with Curves: Create a Curves Adjustment Layer. Double-click the black, gray, or white eyedroppers within the Curves panel to sample the corresponding shadow, midtone, or highlight from your reference swatches, then click the matching tonal area on your original product to map the color over.
Step 4: Masking: Invert the Curves layer mask to black (Ctrl+I or Cmd+I) and use a white brush to paint the color edit strictly onto the targeted parts of the product. 
YouTube
·Adobe Asia Pacific
Method 3: Automated Browser Tools
If you want to quickly align the overall tone of two photos without manual masking, web platforms like Imagen AI offer a Color Match Two Photos tool. You can upload the product photo and the reference shot, and the algorithm will automatically match the average tone and contrast across individual color channels. Note that this matches global color statistics rather than specific objects, so it works best if the layout and framing of both images are roughly similar.
